title: Proverbs, Chapter 11 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 11 on folios 413r, 413v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 11 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 413r, 413v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>מֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭רְמָה תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶ֖בֶן שְׁלֵמָ֣ה רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃ <sup>2</sup>בָּֽא־זָ֭דוֹן וַיָּבֹ֣א קָל֑וֹן וְֽאֶת־צְנוּעִ֥ים חָכְמָֽה׃ <sup>3</sup>תֻּמַּ֣ת יְשָׁרִ֣ים תַּנְחֵ֑ם וְסֶ֖לֶף בּוֹגְדִ֣ים ושדם [יְשָׁדֵּֽם׃] <sup>4</sup>לֹא־יוֹעִ֣יל ה֭וֹן בְּי֣וֹם עֶבְרָ֑ה וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה תַּצִּ֥יל מִמָּֽוֶת׃ <sup>5</sup>צִדְקַ֣ת תָּ֭מִים תְּיַשֵּׁ֣ר דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְרִשְׁעָת֗וֹ יִפֹּ֥ל רָשָֽׁע׃ <sup>6</sup>צִדְקַ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים תַּצִּילֵ֑ם וּ֝בְהַוַּ֗ת בֹּגְדִ֥ים יִלָּכֵֽדוּ׃ <sup>7</sup>בְּמ֤וֹת אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע תֹּאבַ֣ד תִּקְוָ֑ה וְתוֹחֶ֖לֶת אוֹנִ֣ים אָבָֽדָה׃ <sup>8</sup>צַ֭דִּיק מִצָּרָ֣ה נֶחֱלָ֑ץ וַיָּבֹ֖א רָשָׁ֣ע תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight. <sup>2</sup>When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom. <sup>3</sup>The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them. <sup>4</sup>Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death. <sup>5</sup>The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness. <sup>6</sup>The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in their own naughtiness. <sup>7</sup>When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust men perisheth. <sup>8</sup>The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>בְּפֶ֗ה חָ֭נֵף יַשְׁחִ֣ת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וּ֝בְדַ֗עַת צַדִּיקִ֥ים יֵחָלֵֽצוּ׃ <sup>10</sup>בְּט֣וּב צַ֭דִּיקִים תַּעֲלֹ֣ץ קִרְיָ֑ה וּבַאֲבֹ֖ד רְשָׁעִ֣ים רִנָּֽה׃ <sup>11</sup>בְּבִרְכַּ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים תָּר֣וּם קָ֑רֶת וּבְפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תֵּהָרֵֽס׃ <sup>12</sup>בָּז־לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ חֲסַר־לֵ֑ב וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנ֣וֹת יַחֲרִֽישׁ׃ <sup>13</sup>הוֹלֵ֣ךְ רָ֭כִיל מְגַלֶּה־סּ֑וֹד וְנֶאֱמַן־ר֝֗וּחַ מְכַסֶּ֥ה דָבָֽר׃ <sup>14</sup>בְּאֵ֣ין תַּ֭חְבֻּלוֹת יִפָּל־עָ֑ם וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ׃ <sup>15</sup>רַע־יֵ֭רוֹעַ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וְשֹׂנֵ֖א תֹקְעִ֣ים בּוֹטֵֽחַ׃ <sup>16</sup>אֵֽשֶׁת־חֵ֭ן תִּתְמֹ֣ךְ כָּב֑וֹד וְ֝עָרִיצִ֗ים יִתְמְכוּ־עֹֽשֶׁר׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>An hypocrite with his mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered. <sup>10</sup>When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting. <sup>11</sup>By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked. <sup>12</sup>He that is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holdeth his peace. <sup>13</sup>A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. <sup>14</sup>Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety. <sup>15</sup>He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure. <sup>16</sup>A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong men retain riches.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>גֹּמֵ֣ל נַ֭פְשׁוֹ אִ֣ישׁ חָ֑סֶד וְעֹכֵ֥ר שְׁ֝אֵר֗וֹ אַכְזָרִֽי׃ <sup>18</sup>רָשָׁ֗ע עֹשֶׂ֥ה פְעֻלַּת־שָׁ֑קֶר וְזֹרֵ֥עַ צְ֝דָקָ֗ה שֶׂ֣כֶר אֱמֶֽת׃ <sup>19</sup>כֵּן־צְדָקָ֥ה לְחַיִּ֑ים וּמְרַדֵּ֖ף רָעָ֣ה לְמוֹתֽוֹ׃ <sup>20</sup>תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה עִקְּשֵׁי־לֵ֑ב וּ֝רְצוֹנ֗וֹ תְּמִ֣ימֵי דָֽרֶךְ׃ <sup>21</sup>יָ֣ד לְ֭יָד לֹא־יִנָּ֣קֶה רָּ֑ע וְזֶ֖רַע צַדִּיקִ֣ים נִמְלָֽט׃ <sup>22</sup>נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב בְּאַ֣ף חֲזִ֑יר אִשָּׁ֥ה יָ֝פָ֗ה וְסָ֣רַת טָֽעַם׃ <sup>23</sup>תַּאֲוַ֣ת צַדִּיקִ֣ים אַךְ־ט֑וֹב תִּקְוַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים עֶבְרָֽה׃ <sup>24</sup>יֵ֣שׁ מְ֭פַזֵּר וְנוֹסָ֥ף ע֑וֹד וְחוֹשֵׂ֥ךְ מִ֝יֹּ֗שֶׁר אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh. <sup>18</sup>The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward. <sup>19</sup>As righteousness tendeth to life: so he that pursueth evil pursueth it to his own death. <sup>20</sup>They that are of a froward heart are abomination to the LORD: but such as are upright in their way are his delight. <sup>21</sup>Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered. <sup>22</sup>As a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion. <sup>23</sup>The desire of the righteous is only good: but the expectation of the wicked is wrath. <sup>24</sup>There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>נֶֽפֶשׁ־בְּרָכָ֥ה תְדֻשָּׁ֑ן וּ֝מַרְוֶ֗ה גַּם־ה֥וּא יוֹרֶֽא׃ <sup>26</sup>מֹ֣נֵֽעַ בָּ֭ר יִקְּבֻ֣הוּ לְא֑וֹם וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר׃ <sup>27</sup>שֹׁ֣חֵֽר ט֖וֹב יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ רָצ֑וֹן וְדֹרֵ֖שׁ רָעָ֣ה תְבוֹאֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>28</sup>בּוֹטֵ֣חַ בְּ֭עָשְׁרוֹ ה֣וּא יִפֹּ֑ל וְ֝כֶעָלֶ֗ה צַדִּיקִ֥ים יִפְרָֽחוּ׃ <sup>29</sup>עוֹכֵ֣ר בֵּ֭יתוֹ יִנְחַל־ר֑וּחַ וְעֶ֥בֶד אֱ֝וִ֗יל לַחֲכַם־לֵֽב׃ <sup>30</sup>פְּֽרִי־צַ֭דִּיק עֵ֣ץ חַיִּ֑ים וְלֹקֵ֖חַ נְפָשׂ֣וֹת חָכָֽם׃ <sup>31</sup>הֵ֣ן צַ֭דִּיק בָּאָ֣רֶץ יְשֻׁלָּ֑ם אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־רָשָׁ֥ע וְחוֹטֵֽא׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself. <sup>26</sup>He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it. <sup>27</sup>He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him. <sup>28</sup>He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch. <sup>29</sup>He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart. <sup>30</sup>The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise. <sup>31</sup>Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.
